input.answer: If I read it right, I can take the money out without tax six years after the first deposit (three if I've reached retirement age, and I have), and in their 5-year example, with 300 ₪ a month from me and 900 ₪ from the employer, I'd come away with roughly 50 to 66 thousand shekels. But the numbers didn't agree with each other and there was a red minus for tax, so I'll ask you and the fund before I sign anything.

stuck.where: Calculator, screen 3: 'מושכים את הכסף אחרי 5 שנים' with the bar chart
stuck.why: The example opens at 5 years, the year with tax. I didn't know whether to move the little circle to 6, and I don't use sliders, so I stayed with the taxed example.
The bar captions are on the next screen, and at first I thought the 54,000 was my own money. The first bar's number was cut off. The red minus for tax scared me.

stuck.where: Screen 4 sentence: 'לחשבון נכנסים קודם 50,719 ₪, והקרן מעבירה 29,768 ₪ למס הכנסה... 15,794 ₪ מהם חוזרים'
stuck.why: I couldn't tell whether I end up with 50,719, or 66 thousand, or the money that comes back too. A third of it to tax? That's a lot.
The top of the sentence about how much is tax-free was hidden behind the top bar, so I saw only 15,712 ₪ and 20,566 ₪ without knowing what each one was.
The boxes say 2.5% and 7.5%, but the sentence says 300 ₪ and 900 ₪. They don't tell me whose salary that comes from.
